source_text:
Ἄμωμον διάνοιαν καὶ ἀδιάκριτον ἐν ὑπομονῇ ἔγνων ὑμᾶς ἔχοντας, οὐ κατὰ χρῆσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ φύσιν, καθὼς ἐδήλωσέν μοι Πολύβιος, ὁ ἐπίσκοπος ὑμῶν, ὃς παρεγένετο θελήματι θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν Σμύρνῃ καὶ οὕτως μοι συνεχάρη δεδεμένῳ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὥστε με τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ὑμῶν ἐν αὐτῷ θεωρεῖσθαι.
ἀποδεξάμενος οὖν τὴν κατὰ θεὸν εὔνοιαν δἰ αὐτοῦ ἐδόξασα, εὑρὼν ὑμᾶς, ὡς ἔγνων, μιμητὰς ὄντας θεοῦ.
thought_title: Ignatius praises the Trallians' blameless mind and Polybius's visit
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Tralles while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he praises their blameless mind and the visit of their bishop Polybius.
pass_a_gloss: A blameless mind and an undivided one in endurance I came to know you have, not by use but by nature, just as Polybius, your bishop, made clear to me, who came by the will of God and Jesus Christ in Smyrna and in this way rejoiced with me, bound in Christ Jesus, so that I saw the whole multitude of you in him. Having received therefore the goodwill according to God through him, I glorified, having found you, as I came to know, being imitators of God.

choices.why: The adjective describes a mind not torn by doubt or division, matching Ignatius's concern for unity; 'undivided' keeps the negative prefix visible.

choices.term: οὐ κατὰ χρῆσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ φύσιν
choices.english: not by use but by nature
choices.why: The contrast between acquired habit and innate character is central to Ignatius's praise; 'use' preserves the sense of practice or custom.
rejected: not by practice but by disposition
not by habit but by essence

choices.why: Ignatius is a prisoner in chains; 'bound' is the literal state and echoes his self-description as a prisoner in Christ.

choices.term: τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ὑμῶν ἐν αὐτῷ θεωρεῖσθαι
choices.english: I saw the whole multitude of you in him
choices.why: The middle infinitive with 'me' as subject is rendered actively for clarity; 'multitude' preserves the collective body of the church.
rejected: the whole crowd of you was seen in him
I beheld all of you in him

choices.why: The participle with the noun is kept as a clause; 'imitators of God' is a fixed Pauline phrase Ignatius uses for moral likeness.

pass_b_english: I have come to know that you have a blameless and undivided mind in endurance, not by practice but by nature, as Polybius your bishop made clear to me. He came to Smyrna by the will of God and Jesus Christ, and he rejoiced with me, bound as I am in Christ Jesus, so much that I saw your whole multitude in him.
So I received through him your godly goodwill, and I gave glory, finding you, as I have learned, to be imitators of God.

problems.quote: I saw the whole multitude of you in him
problems.source_quote: με τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ὑμῶν ἐν αὐτῷ θεωρεῖσθαι
problems.why: Subject is 'τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ὑμῶν' (the whole multitude of you), with 'με...θεωρεῖσθαι' as infinitive: 'so that I was seen by the whole multitude of you in him' or 'so that the whole multitude of you saw me in him'. English reverses agency: Ignatius is seen by them, not he sees them.
problems.fix: so that I was seen by your whole congregation in him
problems.ruling: με...θεωρεῖσθαι is passive: 'I was seen by the whole multitude of you'; English wrongly makes Ignatius the subject.

problems.why: 'εὔνοια' means 'goodwill, favor'; 'κατὰ θεόν' = 'according to God' or 'godly'. 'Goodwill toward God' suggests the Trallians' goodwill directed to God, but 'εὔνοια' with genitive would be needed. 'κατὰ θεόν' = 'in accordance with God/godly'.
problems.ruling: κατὰ θεόν means 'in accordance with God/godly', not 'toward God'; εὔνοια with genitive needed for direction.

problems.why: 'ἐδόξασα' without object: 'I gave glory/praise' or 'I was glorified'? Aorist active 'I glorified'—but no object 'God' in Greek. English adds 'God'.
problems.ruling: ἐδόξασα lacks explicit object; English adds 'God' without textual warrant, changing meaning.

edits.old: so much that I saw the whole multitude of you in him.
edits.new: so much that I was seen by the whole multitude of you in him.

problems.quote: not by use but by nature
problems.why: 'By use' is unclear; likely means 'by habit/practice' vs. 'by nature.'
problems.fix: Use 'not by practice but by nature.'

edits.old: not by use but by nature
edits.new: not by practice but by nature

fixed: The mistranslation 'not by use but by nature' was corrected to 'not by practice but by nature' to clarify the contrast between habit and nature.

last_rejected.quote: not by use but by nature
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐ κατὰ χρῆσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ φύσιν
last_rejected.why: χρῆσιν means 'habit/practice', not 'use'; φύσιν means 'nature/character', but contrast is 'not acquired habit but innate character'.
last_rejected.fix: not from habit but from character
last_rejected.ruling: χρῆσιν can mean 'use'; φύσιν 'nature' is standard. Rendering within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: so much that I was seen by the whole multitude of you in him
last_rejected.source_quote: ὥστε με τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ὑμῶν ἐν αὐτῷ θεωρεῖσθαι
last_rejected.why: με...θεωρεῖσθαι is passive infinitive 'I to be seen', but ἐν αὐτῷ refers to Polybius, not Christ; 'in him' = in Polybius's report/eyes.
last_rejected.fix: so that the whole multitude of you was seen by me in him
last_rejected.ruling: Passive θεωρεῖσθαι 'I was seen' is correct; ἐν αὐτῷ 'in him' is ambiguous, not a clear mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: ἐδόξασα means 'I glorified/praised [God]', not 'I gave glory' as if transferring it; standard sense is 'I gave thanks/praised'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'I gave glory' is a valid rendering of ἐδόξασα; not a meaning change or loss, just a phrasing preference.

polish.changed: Clarified that Ignatius himself saw the whole multitude in Polybius, not that he was seen by them, and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.

notes.why: Polybius identified as bishop only in 3.1; later just 'your bishop' or 'him' in 3.3.
notes.fix: Clarify in 3.3 that 'your bishop' refers to Polybius.
